cases.name: pow-and-log2-are-exact-where-they-can-be
cases.description: pow with a whole exponent goes through repeated squaring rather than exp(y * log(x)), and log2 reads the exponent of a power of two rather than dividing two logarithms. Both are the difference between 1000 and 999.9999999999999, and a port that reaches for its host's library gets the second one.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="pow(2, 53) == 9007199254740992" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="pow(10, 15) == 1000000000000000" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="pow(2, -2) == 0.25" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="pow(7, 0) == 1" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="pow(9, 0.5) == 3" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="pow(-2, 3) == -8" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="log2(1) == 0" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="log2(512) == 9" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C8"><gen if="log2(0.25) == -2" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C9"><gen if="log10(1000000) == 6" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>p2_53=${{C0}} p10_15=${{C1}} p_neg=${{C2}} p_zero=${{C3}} p_half=${{C4}} p_negbase=${{C5}} l2_1=${{C6}} l2_512=${{C7}} l2_quarter=${{C8}} l10_1e6=${{C9}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: p2_53=ok p10_15=ok p_neg=ok p_zero=ok p_half=ok p_negbase=ok l2_1=ok l2_512=ok l2_quarter=ok l10_1e6=ok

cases.name: atan2-covers-all-four-quadrants
cases.description: atan2 is the one trigonometric function whose answer depends on the SIGNS of both arguments, so a port that forwards to a two-argument arctangent with the arguments the other way round passes every first-quadrant test and fails the other three. Read in whole degrees on purpose: comparing the raw radians against radians(45) would pin an accident of the last bit rather than the quadrant.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(1, 1))) == 45" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(1, -1))) == 135" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(-1, -1))) == -135" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(-1, 1))) == -45" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(1, 0))) == 90" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(-1, 0))) == -90" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(0, -1))) == 180" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="round(degrees(atan2(0, 1))) == 0" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>q1=${{C0}} q2=${{C1}} q3=${{C2}} q4=${{C3}} up=${{C4}} down=${{C5}} left=${{C6}} right=${{C7}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: q1=ok q2=ok q3=ok q4=ok up=ok down=ok left=ok right=ok

cases.name: nan-and-infinity-behave-as-ieee-says
cases.description: An undefined answer must not quietly become zero and an overflow must not quietly become the largest double, because either one turns a broken config into a plausible file. The property that pins it is the one every language shares and none of them advertise: a NaN is not equal to itself, and EVERY comparison against it is false — so a row driven by such a condition falls through to the last branch rather than taking the first.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="sqrt(-1) != sqrt(-1)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="!(sqrt(-1) > 0)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="!(sqrt(-1) < 0)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="!(sqrt(-1) == 0)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="1 / 0 > 100000000000000000000" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="log(0) < -100000000000000000000" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="0 / 0 != 0" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="abs(0 - 1 / 0) > 100000000000000000000" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>ne_self=${{C0}} not_gt=${{C1}} not_lt=${{C2}} not_eq0=${{C3}} div0_inf=${{C4}} log0_neginf=${{C5}} zero_over_zero=${{C6}} abs_inf=${{C7}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: ne_self=ok not_gt=ok not_lt=ok not_eq0=ok div0_inf=ok log0_neginf=ok zero_over_zero=ok abs_inf=ok

cases.name: the-list-functions-over-one-split-string
cases.description: split turns one field into a list and everything after it reads that list: the aggregates, the positional one, and join going back the other way. Three of these are where a port diverges while the rest still pass — the median of an EVEN count is the mean of the middle two, stddev is the POPULATION one divided by n rather than n-1, and splitting the empty string gives no elements rather than one empty one.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="min(split('9,3,27', ',')) == 3" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="max(split('9,3,27', ',')) == 27" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="sum(split('9,3,27', ',')) == 39" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="count(split('9,3,27', ',')) == 3" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="at(split('9,3,27', ','), 0) == 9" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="at(split('9,3,27', ','), 1) == 3" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="mean(split('2,4,6', ',')) == 4" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="median(split('9,3,27', ',')) == 9" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C8"><gen if="median(split('1,2,3,4', ',')) == 2.5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C9"><gen if="stddev(split('2,4,6', ',')) == sqrt(8 / 3)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C10"><gen if="join(split('9,3,27', ','), '-') == '9-3-27'" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C11"><gen if="count(split('', ',')) == 0" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>min=${{C0}} max=${{C1}} sum=${{C2}} count=${{C3}} at0=${{C4}} at1=${{C5}} mean=${{C6}} median_odd=${{C7}} median_even=${{C8}} stddev=${{C9}} join=${{C10}} empty=${{C11}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: min=ok max=ok sum=ok count=ok at0=ok at1=ok mean=ok median_odd=ok median_even=ok stddev=ok join=ok empty=ok

cases.name: precedence-holds-when-functions-are-mixed-in
cases.description: A call binds tighter than any operator, and the operators keep their own order around it. Every line here has a second reading that a hand-written parser produces by accident, and the second reading gives a different number — which is the point: the check cannot pass by luck.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="2 + 3 * abs(-4) == 14" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="(2 + 3) * abs(-4) == 20" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="0 - abs(-4) == -4" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="abs(2 - 5) * 2 == 6" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="10 - 2 - 3 == 5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="2 * 3 % 4 == 2" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="!(1 > 2) && 3 > 2" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="min(1, 2) + max(3, 4) == 5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C8"><gen if="round(1.5) * round(2.5) == 6" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C9"><gen if="sqrt(pow(3, 2) + pow(4, 2)) == 5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C10"><gen if="1 + 1 == 2 && 2 * 2 == 4" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C11"><gen if="(2 + 2 == 4 ? 10 : 20) == 10" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>times_before_plus=${{C0}} parens_win=${{C1}} minus_before_call=${{C2}} arg_is_an_expression=${{C3}} minus_is_left_associative=${{C4}} mod_binds_like_times=${{C5}} not_binds_tightest=${{C6}} two_calls_one_sum=${{C7}} calls_then_multiply=${{C8}} pythagoras=${{C9}} comparison_is_last=${{C10}} ternary_after_math=${{C11}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: times_before_plus=ok parens_win=ok minus_before_call=ok arg_is_an_expression=ok minus_is_left_associative=ok mod_binds_like_times=ok not_binds_tightest=ok two_calls_one_sum=ok calls_then_multiply=ok pythagoras=ok comparison_is_last=ok ternary_after_math=ok

cases.name: comparing-a-whole-number-against-a-float
cases.description: The rule the docs state, made checkable: while both sides are whole the comparison is exact, and one float anywhere drops the WHOLE comparison to floating point. So the big number here compares as equal to a float it is not equal to — and that is correct, not a bug, because there is no exact ordering between a 64-bit integer and a double that is not one. Euclidean % is pinned on a negative DIVISOR too: the usual patch for a negative dividend, ((a % b) + b) % b, gets that one wrong.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="2 == 2.0" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="2 < 2.5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="2.5 > 2" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="!(9007199254740993 > 9007199254740992.0)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="max(9007199254740993, 1) == 9007199254740993" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="min(9007199254740993, 1) == 1" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="(0 - 7) % 3 == 2" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="7 % (0 - 3) == 1" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C8"><gen if="7.5 % 2 == 1.5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C9"><gen if="7 / 2 == 3.5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C10"><gen if="3 in [1, 2, 3]" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C11"><gen if="!(4 in [1, 2, 3])" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C12"><gen if="1 + 2 in [1, 2, 3]" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C13"><gen if="(1 > 2 ? 10 : 3 > 2 ? 20 : 30) == 20" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>whole_eq_float=${{C0}} whole_lt_float=${{C1}} float_gt_whole=${{C2}} float_drops_exactness=${{C3}} max_stays_exact=${{C4}} min_stays_exact=${{C5}} mod_negative_left=${{C6}} mod_negative_right=${{C7}} mod_float=${{C8}} div_makes_float=${{C9}} in_numbers=${{C10}} not_in=${{C11}} in_after_math=${{C12}} chained_ternary=${{C13}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: whole_eq_float=ok whole_lt_float=ok float_gt_whole=ok float_drops_exactness=ok max_stays_exact=ok min_stays_exact=ok mod_negative_left=ok mod_negative_right=ok mod_float=ok div_makes_float=ok in_numbers=ok not_in=ok in_after_math=ok chained_ternary=ok

cases.name: math-reads-a-column-not-only-a-literal
cases.description: Every check above is a constant folded before the run. Here the operand is a COLUMN, so the value arrives as text and has to read as a number on the way into each function — the step where a port that parses eagerly and one that parses lazily part company.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="Amount"><gen type="text" value="100,250,7" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="Doubled"><gen if="Amount * 2 == 200" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="no"/></sequence><sequence name="Near"><gen if="abs(Amount - 250) < 1" type="text" value="mid"/><gen type="text" value="other"/></sequence><sequence name="Digits"><gen if="len(Amount) == 3" type="text" value="three"/><gen if="len(Amount) == 1" type="text" value="one"/><gen type="text" value="other"/></sequence><sequence name="Root"><gen if="round(sqrt(Amount)) == 10" type="text" value="ten"/><gen type="text" value="not"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Amount}} doubled=${{Doubled}} near=${{Near}} digits=${{Digits}} root=${{Root}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-record-number-is-a-number
cases.description: _count and _total are the two builtins arithmetic reaches for, and the boundary is the whole point: on record 3 of 6, _count > _total / 2 is false, because three is not more than three. A port that rounds the division, or compares as text, gets a different row here and nowhere else.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="Parity"><gen if="_count % 2 == 0" type="text" value="even"/><gen type="text" value="odd"/></sequence><sequence name="Half"><gen if="_count > _total / 2" type="text" value="late"/><gen type="text" value="early"/></sequence><sequence name="Quarter"><gen if="floor(_total / 4) == 1" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="Square"><gen if="_count == pow(round(sqrt(_count)), 2)" type="text" value="square"/><gen type="text" value="not"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>n=${{_count}}/${{_total}} ${{Parity}} ${{Half}} quarter=${{Quarter}} ${{Square}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-conditional-chain-where-the-math-picks-the-branch
cases.description: Five branches in order, each a logarithm, so the value that lands on a boundary decides between two of them: log10(1000) is 3 exactly and takes the branch above, log10(999) is not and takes the one below. This is the landmark case turned into a row — if log10 were 2.9999999999999996, the file would differ rather than a test failing.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="7" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="Amount"><gen type="text" value="3,50,100,999,1000,7500,20000" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="Band"><gen if="log10(Amount) >= 4" type="text" value="huge"/><gen if="log10(Amount) >= 3" type="text" value="large"/><gen if="log10(Amount) >= 2" type="text" value="medium"/><gen if="log10(Amount) >= 1" type="text" value="small"/><gen type="text" value="tiny"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Amount}} -> ${{Band}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: filter-narrows-a-pool-by-arithmetic
cases.description: filter= is the other place an expression runs, and it runs once per candidate rather than once per row. Three filters over one pool: a comparison against a column of this row, a distance, and a remainder. Each drawn member is then read back in an if= that restates the filter's own promise, so a divergence names itself instead of showing up as a different number.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="pf" local="en" mode="memory"><pool name="Boxes" count="6"><sequence name="cap"><gen type="text" value="10,20,30,40,50,60" order="sequential"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="Need"><gen type="text" value="15,45" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="Fits"><gen type="pool" value="Boxes" filter="cap >= Need"/></sequence><sequence name="Near"><gen type="pool" value="Boxes" filter="abs(cap - Need) <= 5"/></sequence><sequence name="Round"><gen type="pool" value="Boxes" filter="cap % 20 == 0"/></sequence><sequence name="V1"><gen if="Fits.cap >= Need" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="V2"><gen if="abs(Near.cap - Need) <= 5" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="V3"><gen if="Round.cap % 20 == 0" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>need=${{Need}} fits=${{Fits.cap}} ${{V1}} near=${{Near.cap}} ${{V2}} round=${{Round.cap}} ${{V3}}</data></line></block></tdc>
expected: need=15 fits=40 ok near=20 ok round=40 ok
need=45 fits=50 ok near=40 ok round=20 ok
need=15 fits=20 ok near=10 ok round=40 ok
need=45 fits=50 ok near=50 ok round=40 ok
need=15 fits=60 ok near=20 ok round=40 ok
need=45 fits=50 ok near=50 ok round=20 ok

cases.name: gauss-clamp-and-lerp-are-the-compositions-they-claim
cases.description: Three functions that are pure compositions of arithmetic already pinned elsewhere, so what needs pinning is the CHOICE inside each. gauss squares with a multiplication rather than pow, which is exact under IEEE-754 where pow is not — the same_as_exp_pow row proves the two agree anyway, so a config that switches to gauss keeps its bytes. clamp says what happens when the bounds are handed over backwards, because a port that reaches for its host's clamp gets an exception there instead of an answer. The last lerp row is the one that separates the two textbook spellings: a + (b - a) * t returns 0.003631319229647878 for that pair while a * (1 - t) + b * t returns the endpoint itself, and over 200,000 random pairs the naive form misses the endpoint 41 per cent of the time.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="gauss(3, 3, 1.5) == 1" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="gauss(1, 3, 1.5) == gauss(5, 3, 1.5)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="gauss(1.7, 3.2, 0.9) == exp(-pow((1.7 - 3.2) / 0.9, 2))" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="gauss(-4, 0, 2) == exp(-4)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="clamp(1, 2, 4) == 2" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="clamp(3, 2, 4) == 3" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="clamp(9, 2, 4) == 4" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="clamp(5, 8, 2) == 2" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C8"><gen if="clamp(-0.5, -0.25, 0.25) == -0.25" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C9"><gen if="lerp(10, 20, 0) == 10" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C10"><gen if="lerp(10, 20, 1) == 20" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C11"><gen if="lerp(10, 20, 0.5) == 15" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C12"><gen if="lerp(10, 20, 2) == 30" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C13"><gen if="lerp(10, 20, -1) == 0" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C14"><gen if="lerp(0.8016350265761529, 0.0036313192296478915, 1) == 0.0036313192296478915" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>peak=${{C0}} symmetric=${{C1}} same_as_exp_pow=${{C2}} known_value=${{C3}} below=${{C4}} inside=${{C5}} above=${{C6}} inverted=${{C7}} negative=${{C8}} t0=${{C9}} t1=${{C10}} mid=${{C11}} extrapolates=${{C12}} extrapolates_back=${{C13}} endpoint_exact=${{C14}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: hash-is-the-same-stream-in-every-implementation
cases.description: hash(n, salt) replaces the shader sin-trick a config writes for a per-row random coefficient. It is cyrb128 + sfc32 — the PRNG the rest of TDC runs on — keyed by the IEEE-754 BIT PATTERNS of the two arguments rather than by their decimal spellings. That choice is what the last row tests: the shortest decimal form of a double is not the same string in every language, so a port that builds the key from digits drifts on a fractional salt while passing every whole-number row above it. The three published values fail immediately for a port that mixes differently at all.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="1" seed="m" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="C0"><gen if="hash(1, 12.9) == 0.41771199833601713" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C1"><gen if="hash(2, 12.9) == 0.5759327965788543" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C2"><gen if="hash(1, 78.2) == 0.36098611587658525" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C3"><gen if="hash(7, 3) >= 0 && hash(7, 3) < 1" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C4"><gen if="hash(5, 1) != hash(5, 2)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C5"><gen if="hash(5, 1) != hash(6, 1)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C6"><gen if="hash(5, 1) == hash(5, 1)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C7"><gen if="hash(0, 1) != hash(0 - 0.0, 1) ? 1 : 1" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence><sequence name="C8"><gen if="hash(3, 0.1 + 0.2) == hash(3, 0.30000000000000004)" type="text" value="ok"/><gen type="text" value="WRONG"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>v1=${{C0}} v2=${{C1}} salted=${{C2}} in_range=${{C3}} salt_separates=${{C4}} n_separates=${{C5}} repeatable=${{C6}} zero_ok=${{C7}} fractional_salt=${{C8}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: noise-is-smooth-value-noise-over-the-same-hash
cases.description: noise(t, scale, salt) draws an independent value every `scale` rows and eases between them, which is what a drifting baseline needs and what three modulated sines cannot give: measured on 4096 samples, the sines put 74.6 per cent of their power in three frequency bins and this puts 51.5. The rows that matter here are the lattice ones: interpolating with a*(1-u) + b*u rather than a + (b-a)*u makes noise at a lattice point EXACTLY equal to hash there, so a cell boundary is continuous to the last bit rather than to within an ulp — a port that picks the other spelling passes the range and midpoint rows and fails these three. The midpoint row pins the easing: smoothstep(0.5) is exactly one half, so the centre of a cell is the plain average of its ends.
